title: Up and Down
full_review:
The absorbing and kaleidoscopic "Up & Down" (Sony Classics) deftly interweaves several plot strands to create a vivid picture of the present-day, post-communist Czech Republic.

The myriad characters include black-market smugglers who inadvertently steal a baby and a likable but loutish ex-soccer hooligan now on probation (Jiri Machacek) whose wife (Natasa Burger) is obsessed with having a child and ultimately "buys" the abducted infant.

Meanwhile, a seriously ill college professor (Jan Triska) summons both his grown son (Petr Forman) from Australia and his long-estranged wife (Emilia Vasaryova), after an absence of many years, to meet the woman (Ingrid Timkova) he's been living with -- and by whom he has sired a daughter -- and hopes to marry provided the first wife will divorce him.

Jan Hrebejk's film -- shot almost documentary style in actual Prague apartments and streets -- brilliantly deals with heavy-duty issues like cultural assimilation, national identity, love and hate, and the effects of globalization, but does so in an entertaining Altmanesque way and ties the disparate story elements together neatly by the conclusion.

The film contains rough, profane and crude language, racial epithets, a brief but sordid sexual situation, and a short scene of violence with some blood. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
